monuments.name: Grossmünster (Romanesque Twin-Towered Cathedral)
monuments.architect: Romanesque Twin Sandstone Towers & Scarlet Octagonal Domes (1100–1220 / 1787)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Romanesque Twin Sandstone Towers & Scarlet Octagonal Domes (1100–1220 / 1787)
monuments.fact: Legend holds that Charlemagne founded Grossmünster where his horse knelt over the tombs of Zurich’s patron saints Felix and Regula. From its pulpit in 1519, Huldrych Zwingli launched the Swiss Reformation; its iconic twin Neo-Gothic domed helmets were added in 1787.

monuments.name: Fraumünster Abbey & St. Peter’s Clock Tower
monuments.architect: Gothic Choir with Marc Chagall Windows, Patinated Copper Spire & 8.7m Golden Clock Dial
monuments.architecturalStyle: Gothic Choir with Marc Chagall Windows, Patinated Copper Spire & 8.7m Golden Clock Dial
monuments.fact: Founded in 853 by King Louis the German for aristocratic women, Fraumünster’s slender blue-green spire rises beside St. Peter’s Church—whose 1534 tower sports the largest church clock face in Europe at 8.7 meters in diameter.

monuments.name: Zürich Hauptbahnhof (1871 Wanner Portal & Underground S-Bahn Hub)
monuments.architect: Jakob Friedrich Wanner Triumphal Sandstone Arch & Multi-Level Underground S-Bahn Halls
monuments.architecturalStyle: Jakob Friedrich Wanner Triumphal Sandstone Arch & Multi-Level Underground S-Bahn Halls
monuments.fact: Site of Switzerland’s first railway in 1847 (the "Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn" to Baden), Zürich HB features Jakob Friedrich Wanner’s 1871 sandstone triumphal arch above three subterranean through-stations serving over 2,900 trains daily.

monuments.name: ETH Zürich Semper Building & 1889 UBS Polybahn Funicular
monuments.architect: Neoclassical Acropolis Palace, Gustav Gull Cupola (1918) & Crimson Polybahn Viaduct
monuments.architecturalStyle: Neoclassical Acropolis Palace, Gustav Gull Cupola (1918) & Crimson Polybahn Viaduct
monuments.fact: Designed by Gottfried Semper in 1864 atop the Zürichberg terrace (where Albert Einstein studied and taught) and linked to Central down on the Limmat by the crimson 1889 Polybahn funicular.

monuments.name: Opernhaus Zürich & Sechseläutenplatz
monuments.architect: Neo-Baroque White Stone Portico, Busts of Mozart & Wagner, and Copper Auditorium Roof
monuments.architecturalStyle: Neo-Baroque White Stone Portico, Busts of Mozart & Wagner, and Copper Auditorium Roof
monuments.fact: Built in just 16 months in 1890–1891 by Viennese theater architects Fellner & Helmer after the Aktientheater burned down, Opernhaus Zürich was the first opera house in Europe with electric lighting and anchors the Valser quartzite expanse of Sechseläutenplatz.

monuments.name: Prime Tower & Hardbrücke Viaduct (Zürich-West)
monuments.architect: 126m Faceted Blue-Green Glass Polygon Tower & Historic Brick Maag Gear Hall
monuments.architecturalStyle: 126m Faceted Blue-Green Glass Polygon Tower & Historic Brick Maag Gear Hall
monuments.fact: Designed by Annette Gigon and Mike Guyer on the former Maag gear-factory grounds beside Hardbrücke station, the 126-meter octagonal-faceted Prime Tower catalyzed the transformation of industrial Kreis 5 into Zürich-West.

monuments.name: Kunsthaus Zürich (Moser Hall & Chipperfield Building)
monuments.architect: Jura Limestone Fluted Facade, Brass Fins & Underground Art Passage across Heimplatz
monuments.architecturalStyle: Jura Limestone Fluted Facade, Brass Fins & Underground Art Passage across Heimplatz
monuments.fact: Home to Switzerland’s largest art collection (from Alberto Giacometti and Ferdinand Hodler to Dadaism, born nearby at Cabaret Voltaire in 1916), uniting Karl Moser’s 1910 Villa with David Chipperfield’s 2021 Jura-limestone wing.

monuments.name: Uetliberg Kulm Observation Tower & Hotel Uto Kulm (870m)
monuments.architect: 72m Triangular Steel Lattice Lookout Tower, Panoramic Platform & 186m TV Mast
monuments.architecturalStyle: 72m Triangular Steel Lattice Lookout Tower, Panoramic Platform & 186m TV Mast
monuments.fact: Rising 464 meters above Lake Zurich at 870m elevation and reached by the electric S10 Uetlibergbahn (opened 1875), the 72m triangular steel lookout tower commands a 360° panorama from the Limmat Valley to the Bernese and Glarus Alps.
